reviews.title: Facebook has lost its way
reviews.text: Facebook is definitely not what it used to be, and honestly, it’s getting frustrating. I remember when Facebook was about connecting with family, friends, meeting new people, and actually being social. Now it feels like one giant advertisement. My feed is constantly filled with posts from people I don’t even know, while I barely see anything from my actual friends and family. You have thousands of friends and followers, yet only a small fraction ever see what you post unless you pay to promote it, and even then there’s no guarantee they’ll see it. Facebook encourages you to share posts with multiple groups using its own features, then turns around and restricts you for sharing too much. You try adding people you have mutual friends with, and Facebook won’t let you. You try messaging people who are literally already on your friends list, and somehow you get restricted from doing that too. Posts get flagged for things you see other people posting every single day, yet somehow sexually explicit content slips through. And don’t even get me started on the blue checkmark. What used to represent verification now feels more like another subscription they’re trying to sell you. I’ve paid for verification, and it certainly hasn’t stopped these ridiculous restrictions. The whole thing is becoming a contradiction. Facebook claims to be about bringing people together, but it keeps putting limitations on how people can actually connect. They did an amazing job making the platform addictive, but I genuinely believe people are getting tired of it. Other social media apps are starting to look more appealing because people want actual connections, not constant advertisements, restrictions, and algorithms deciding who gets to see what. I understand the need to prevent spam and protect users, but there needs to be a better balance between protecting the community and punishing people for normal social interactions. At this point, I have to ask, what’s the purpose of a social networking platform that keeps making it harder to network and socialize? Facebook seriously needs to remember what made people love it in the first place.
